security_audit.summary: The static backtick findings are Markdown formatting and documentation examples, not Ruby backtick execution or hidden shell interpolation. No prompt-injection language was found in SKILL.md. The remaining concern is the intended broad belt CLI permission, which can execute external commands and send prompts or image URLs to hosted services.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed Bash patterns to the needed belt subcommands, such as login, app store, and app run, if the platform supports narrower patterns.
State that prompts, image URLs, and generated assets may be sent to inference.sh and model providers.
Prefer version-pinned install instructions or a reviewed dependency reference instead of a mutable raw GitHub branch link.

semantic_findings.title: Broad External CLI Permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill grants Bash access to all belt subcommands while examples send prompts and image URLs to hosted image apps. This is intended behavior, but users need clear consent before external command execution and data transfer.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools declaration directly permits Bash(belt *), and the quick start and editing examples show belt commands using external hosted apps. This is an operational risk, not evidence of malicious intent.

content.user_title: Generate AI Images with Hosted Models
content.value_statement: Creating model-specific image commands can be slow and inconsistent. This skill provides belt CLI examples for generation, editing, stitching, and upscaling.
actual_capabilities: Lists hosted image model app IDs for OpenAI, FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, Pruna, and Topaz.
Provides belt CLI examples for text-to-image generation with prompt inputs.
Shows image editing workflows that pass image URLs to supported model apps.
Shows upscaling and image stitching workflows for hosted image apps.
Points users to the inference.sh image app catalog and documentation.
limitations: Requires the external belt CLI and a configured inference.sh account.
Sends prompts and image URLs to external hosted model services when commands run.
Does not verify current model availability, pricing, or output quality.
Placeholder image URLs must be replaced with accessible user-provided URLs.

use_cases.title: Product Visual Mockups
use_cases.description: Create product photo prompts and choose model examples for catalog images, ads, or pitch materials.

use_cases.title: Concept Art Exploration
use_cases.description: Compare image model options for scenes, characters, posters, and style experiments before production work.

use_cases.title: Image Operations
use_cases.description: Use documented commands for upscaling, stitching, and editing image assets through hosted apps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a product image prompt for a ceramic mug on a clean studio background. Recommend one belt app from this skill.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the listed models for a poster with readable text. Recommend the best option and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Edit an Existing Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an image editing workflow that changes the background of my product photo to a beach at sunset.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Step Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow that generates a campaign image, tests two model choices, then upscales the best result.

output_examples.input: Generate a studio product image for sneakers.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a hosted generation app, prepares a concise product prompt, and describes the belt action to run.

output_examples.input: Change the background of a product photo.
output_examples.output: The skill selects an editing-capable model and explains which image URL and background instruction the command should include.
The skill points to the Topaz upscaler app and explains how to provide the image URL for enhancement.

best_practices: Confirm model cost and data policy before running any belt command.
Use accessible, non-sensitive image URLs when testing editing or upscaling examples.
Start with a focused prompt, then adjust model-specific options after reviewing output.
anti_patterns: Do not submit confidential images or prompts unless provider terms allow that use.
Do not run install commands from mutable remote links without review.
Do not assume every listed model supports editing, LoRA, upscaling, or text rendering.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images directly?
faq.answer: No. It guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to use the external belt CLI with hosted image apps.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples require the belt CLI and any account or authentication needed by inference.sh.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes, when the chosen model supports editing and the input image is available through a URL.

faq.question: Which model should I use first?
faq.answer: Use GPT-Image-2 or FLUX examples for general generation. Use Topaz for upscaling workflows.

faq.question: Are generated results deterministic?
faq.answer: No. Hosted image models can vary by prompt, settings, model version, and provider behavior.

faq.question: Is this safe for private assets?
faq.answer: Use caution. Running the examples can send prompts and image URLs to external services.
